questions.question: Why does the prologue open with a scene in the Sahara, when the story immediately returns to childhood?
answers: Because the Sahara is more important than the castle in Saint-Maurice
Because the crash and the rescue foreshadow the image from which "The Little Prince" would grow
Because Antoine only then learned to write
Because the Bedouin is the main character of the book
questions.explanation: The prologue links the desert crash with the future fairy tale about a pilot and a golden-haired boy — and with the memory of a brother who "never grew up".

questions.question: What did the nickname "Sun King" mean in Antoine's childhood?
answers: That he was the official heir to the throne of France
That the household saw him as a golden-haired boy of royal temperament with a "throne"
That he ruled the castle instead of his mother
That he was forbidden to play in the attic
questions.explanation: The household called him that; he carried a green lacquered little chair like a throne and sat wherever his mother stopped.

questions.question: What did Antoine learn on his first flight in Ambérieu?
answers: That his mother always lets him fly
That the sky could become the place where he wants to spend his life — even though he boarded by lying
That the Legion of Honour awaits twelve-year-olds
That Wróblewski refused to take off
questions.explanation: The twelve-year-old lied about his mother's consent; in the air he felt freedom and a calling he could not yet name.

questions.question: How does François's death later connect with "The Little Prince"?
answers: François wrote the first version of the fairy tale
The brother's farewell words and gesture return in the golden-haired boy's farewell; the figure also carries the memory of a brother who did not grow up
François was the model for Consuelo
Antoine forgot his brother and invented the ending from scratch
questions.explanation: The narrative stresses that the words about the "old bark" and the fall "the way a tree falls" return in the fairy tale; François is also the core of the figure.

questions.question: Who is the rose in the interpretation given in the text — and why does it matter?
answers: The mother Marie — because she read Andersen
Consuelo — capricious, unique; only a fairy tale allows Antoine to say tenderly what he could not in life
Antoine's sister
A metaphor for the Simoun aeroplane
questions.explanation: Antoine never hid that the rose was Consuelo; the stormy relationship takes on a tender and gentle form in the fairy tale.

questions.question: Why did Antoine refuse to change the ending of "The Little Prince"?
answers: Because the publishers wanted a longer book
Because the death scene was a transfer of the most intimate memory of François — a farewell, not an ornament
Because Consuelo wrote that ending
Because copyright law forbade changes
questions.explanation: The publishers feared the boy's death; Antoine defended a scene written with words carried for a quarter of a century — the fairy tale was a testament and a farewell.
